introduction: Today we celebrate the Transfiguration of the Lord. Jesus goes up the mountain to pray, and as he prays his face is changed and his clothes become dazzling white. Moses and Elijah speak with him about his departure in Jerusalem, and the Father's voice says, This is my beloved Son; listen to him. Peter writes that he was an eyewitness of Christ's majesty. Let us listen to the beloved Son, and let his light shine in our hearts.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Father has shown us the glory of his Son. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may listen to the beloved Son and reflect his glory in the world. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who live in darkness: that the light of Christ may rise in their hearts like the morning star. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace in the world, and for all victims of war: that the glory of God may overcome violence and hatred. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are discouraged on their journey: that a glimpse of Christ's glory may give them strength. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may make time to pray and listen to Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, on the holy mountain you revealed the glory of your Son as he prayed. Help us to listen to him and to be transformed by his light. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: As he was praying
reflection.body:
The prophet Daniel sees a vision of heaven: the Ancient of Days on a throne of fire, and "one like a son of man" who comes with the clouds and receives an everlasting kingdom. On the mountain of the Transfiguration, the disciples glimpse that glory in Jesus.

Luke tells us that Jesus took Peter, John and James "up onto the mountain to pray." And it was "As he was praying" that "the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling." In Luke, the Transfiguration happens in prayer. Prayer is where the light of God shines through.

Moses and Elijah appear and speak with Jesus "of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem." The glory of the mountain is linked to the cross that awaits him. The disciples are "heavy with sleep," but they wake and see his glory. Peter wants to stay and build three tents. Then a cloud overshadows them, and a voice says, "This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!" When the voice is gone, "Jesus was found alone."

Peter later remembers this moment: "we didn't follow cunningly devised fables... but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty." He heard the voice "when we were with him on the holy mountain." And he tells us to hold on to God's word "as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts."

Today's feast reminds us of where we are going: to share in the glory of Christ. It also shows us the way: prayer and listening to Jesus. This week, find a quiet time to pray, perhaps before the Blessed Sacrament, and ask the Lord to let his light shine in you.
